title: Overnight Farming
subject: Which map pays most while you sleep

board.title: Overnight Farming — every map per night, in story order

method.summary: The game's own offline run (what it plays when you come back), 8 hours from 23:00 to 07:00, on every story chapter, averaged over 3 nights. Money night: White Kyurem, Tyranitar, Chandelure, Metagross, Gyarados, Garchomp, all Lv 100. Leveling night: White Kyurem, Tyranitar, Chandelure, Metagross at Lv 100 carry while Skuntank and Garchomp level (Lv 50, *1), Garchomp as companion. Simulated with the game's own code on build aa84889c89, with a save past the story (gifts and one-time finds done). A weaker team wins fewer fights a night and can lose to League trainers. Time: each action takes 1.5 s of your absence, for at most 8 hours. After every wild Pokémon it beats, the game spends 4.5 s more: it tries to catch a new species and turns one you own into candy. So a trainer-only map gets about 19,000 actions a night, a route with wild Pokémon 10,000 to 13,000. Gyms are skipped while away: at a chapter's gym the run starts that chapter again. In a League you have beaten, it walks on through the Elite Four and Champion routes and round again, so any of them gives the same night. Your companion gets ×1.3 EXP and, every few KOs (every 20 for a rare), a candy worth three levels of base EXP at its level, so the more wins the better; it reaches the level cap on every map here. Chapters marked as loops share the night (the run moves to the next one at each gym). Captures can't be turned off: a map with fewer wild Pokémon loses less time to them. Money: only trainers pay (30 × their level, ×0.9); wild Pokémon pay nothing. The best maps pack many high-level trainers into a short loop. EXP = wins × EXP per win: every win pays every team member (+10% for one that fought), at half rate while away. Fast maps win more often; League trainers pay far more per win. The ranking is for the leveler that isn't your companion. Level cap: while away, a Pokémon gains at most 12 levels, however much EXP comes in, so the EXP map only matters for high levels and high ranks.

algorithm.goal: Rank every story map by money per night and by EXP per night for a leveler that is not the companion.
algorithm.engine: The game's own offline run at build aa84889c89
steps: Start from a save past the story (gifts and one-time finds done).
Run the offline simulation for 8 hours, 23:00 to 07:00, with each action costing 1.5 s and each wild KO costing 4.5 s more.
Money night: White Kyurem, Tyranitar, Chandelure, Metagross, Gyarados, Garchomp, all Lv 100.
Leveling night: the same four at Lv 100 carry while Skuntank and Garchomp level (Lv 50, *1), Garchomp as companion.
Count money from trainers only: 30 × level × 0.9; wild Pokémon pay nothing.
Count EXP as wins × EXP per win, paid to every member at half rate while away, +10% for the one that fought; the companion gets ×1.3 and candy every few KOs.
Apply the 12-level cap and rank the leveler that is not the companion.

acceptance.money: Only trainers pay, 30 × level × 0.9; wild Pokémon pay nothing.
acceptance.exp: Every win pays every team member, half rate while away, +10% for the one that fought.
acceptance.cap: A Pokémon gains at most 12 levels in one night, so the EXP map only matters at high level and rank.

gameFacts: Each action takes 1.5 s of absence, for at most 8 hours.
After each wild KO the game spends 4.5 s more to try a capture and turn an owned duplicate into candy.
Gyms are skipped while away: at a gym the run restarts the chapter.
A beaten League loops Elite Four + Champion rounds; any of them gives the same night.
Loops share the night, moving to the next loop at each gym.
Money = 30 × trainer level × 0.9; wild Pokémon pay nothing.
EXP = wins × EXP/win; every member is paid, half rate while away, +10% if it fought.
Companion: ×1.3 EXP and a candy every 20 KOs for a rare, worth three levels of base EXP at its level.
Ranking is for the leveler that is not the companion.

uncertain: The OCR of the per-region tables interleaves Johto and Hoenn in two columns; the rows were re-aligned by map order and the money/EXP top lists, which match (Johto League 37.65M / 1.46M, Hoenn League 32.60M / 1.76M).
Sinnoh's first money cell was blank before 533k; 533k is stored for Coal Badge, and the alternative (Coal missing, 533k for Forest Badge) is not used because 14 maps need 14 values.
The xpNeed matrix's verdicts are printed as colour blocks plus short labels; the stored `verdict` concatenates the four rank verdicts in *0/*1/*3/*5 order for the Lv 60–88 rows where they differ.
The board gives no 'from Lv 100' row; the matrix stops at Lv 88 because the 12-level cap reaches 100 from there.
